head.h1: Production Catering in Dubai — Prices, Formats and What You Get

Think of it as catering built around a call sheet: hot meals delivered on time between setups, craft service that keeps energy up through a long shoot day, and a vetted chef who works quietly around cameras, cabling and tight turnarounds. Send your dates and crew size, and promptly during our published business hours you get an itemised proposal.

new_paragraphs: Production catering includes everything needed to keep a working set fed without slowing the shoot: menu design, a vetted chef and crew, on-location cooking or delivery, full setup and cleanup, and disposables where a location has no kitchen. As a production catering company Dubai crews rely on, myCHEF plans around your schedule, not its own — main meals timed to breaks, and craft service topped up between them. A typical day covers a hot breakfast, a proper lunch, and continuous coffee, snacks and cold drinks, with hot dinners added for night shoots. The service covers commercial and film sets, photo shoots, live broadcasts, brand content days and multi-day event builds. Everything is dietary-labelled, because a mixed crew usually brings vegetarian, vegan, halal and allergy needs that cannot hold up a scene.

Meals are timed to your schedule and held hot or cold safely, so a delayed lunch does not become a food-safety problem. Access, parking and load-in are confirmed with your location manager beforehand, so nothing about the catering surprises your crew on the day.

add_block.new_heading: Planning production catering step by step
new_paragraphs: Send your date, guest count and venue — your proposal arrives.
Book production catering about 2 weeks ahead off-peak, and 6 weeks ahead between November and March.
Confirm your menu about 7 days out, when the guest list is firm.
Ask early about allergies and dietary plates — not in the last 48 hours before production catering.
Check the access route before production catering day — setup starts roughly 2 hours ahead.
Plan on roughly 3 hours of service, and add 5% VAT to the total.

new_paragraphs: How much does production catering cost in Dubai?

Production catering starts from around AED 700 per person and is quoted by crew size, number of services a day and menu level. Multi-day shoots are priced per programme, which usually works out better value than day rates.
What is included in production catering?

Included is menu design, a vetted chef and crew, on-location cooking or delivery, setup and cleanup, and disposables where a location has no kitchen. Craft service and dietary options are part of the plan.
Can you handle dietary requirements for a mixed crew?
Yes — every service includes vegetarian and vegan mains, plus halal, gluten-free, dairy-free and nut-free options. All dishes are labelled so crew can grab food fast between setups.
Do you cater remote or desert shoot locations?

Yes. For locations with no facilities the team is fully self-sufficient, bringing its own equipment, power planning, water, disposables and waste management, confirmed with your location manager in advance.
How do I hire or set up a regular production catering arrangement?

Send your shoot dates, crew size and schedule, and you get an itemised proposal, usually within one business day. For repeat or multi-week productions, an ongoing arrangement with consistent menus and simplified billing can be set up.
How far in advance should I book?
Book as early as you can for larger crews and peak periods, though short-notice shoots are turned around regularly. Share your dates and availability is confirmed quickly.

MyCHEF aims to be: vetted chefs, on-schedule service and itemised pricing are the standard. It would sooner earn best production catering Dubai on delivery than claim it, so each shoot and its results speak for themselves.
